title: Longer and Shorter Worksheets for Kindergarten
intro: Teach length comparison by lining up the starting points.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Use the pictured bars or real strips and compare their endpoints from a shared start. Read the labels aloud if needed.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Slide the strips so their left ends line up. Keep both strips straight. Now look at the other ends: the strip that extends farther is longer, and the one that stops first is shorter.

On this worksheet the two bars already start at the same place. Trace each bar from left to right, circle the longer bar, and write its label, A or B, in the answer box.

Ask your student

Which bar reaches farther from the starting line?

If your student needs help

If the student chooses by position, move the strips back to the same starting point.

Choosing and using the worksheet

This activity covers horizontal length comparison only. It does not teach area, weight, capacity, or reading a ruler. Keep those attributes separate when choosing the next worksheet.
